findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, so any nonempty first page raises TypeError when build_cursor generates its cursors. value_from_cursor also returns a number rather than converting it to a datetime for subsequent queries. Use DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversion behavior for this endpoint.

findings.title: Django querysets do not support negative slicing
findings.body: The advanced pagination branch passes a negative cursor offset directly to QuerySet slicing. Django explicitly raises ValueError for negative indexes; it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. An authorized caller supplying a negative offset therefore gets a server error rather than reverse pagination. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or implement reverse traversal using supported queryset operations.

findings.title: Changing existing Redis set keys to sorted sets requires a migration
findings.body: The new ZADD and ZSCAN operations reuse the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous consumer populated with Redis sets. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors on insertion or flushing after deployment, and old and new workers cannot safely share these keys during a rolling deployment. This can stall ingestion and leave buffered spans to expire without being emitted. Introduce a versioned key namespace or an explicit drain/conversion rollout before switching Redis types.

findings.title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
findings.body: The Lua script always truncates segments to 1000 spans, while SpansBuffer still exposes max_segment_spans and the flush-time enforcement of that setting has been removed. A buffer configured with a smaller limit now emits segments above its configured limit, and one configured with a larger limit silently loses spans at 1000 anyway. Pass the configured limit into the script and define the corresponding eviction behavior rather than leaving the public configuration ineffective.
